// unblocked base case of recursive potrf\n\n// Pack rows [s, s+R) of an m x kc block (row-major, stride lda) into P[k][R]\ntemplate <size_t R>\ninline void packSliver(const double* A, const size_t lda, const size_t m, const size_t s,\n                       const size_t kc, double* P) {\n    const size_t rows = std::min(R, m - s);\n    for (size_t k = 0; The changes are only in `cholesky/cholesky.cpp` and `cholesky/CMakeLists.txt`; the executable is still called `cholesky`.\n\n**Timings on this machine** (2× 64-core EPYC 7763, 256 hardware threads, default settings, decomposition time only):\n\n| n | before | after |\n|---|---|---|\n| 512 | – | ~3 ms |\n| 1024 | – | ~3–4 ms |\n| 2048 | 2143 ms (1.3 GFLOPS) | ~11 ms (~160 GFLOPS) |\n| 4096 | – | ~41 ms (~440 GFLOPS) |\n| 8192 | – | ~165–185 ms (~1.1 TFLOPS) |\n| 16384 | – | ~840 ms (~1.75 TFLOPS) |\n\nI only timed the original at n=2048.\n\n**How it works**\n- **Blocked algorithm:** the decomposition now works one block of columns at a time. Each step factors a small diagonal block, solves the column panel below it, then updates the rest of the matrix in tiles.\n- **Fast inner kernel:** the updates run through a vectorized 6×8 matrix-multiply kernel. The panel solve and the diagonal-block factorization reuse it.\n- **Threads keep their tiles:** each tile is always updated by the same thread, so its data stays in that core's cache from step to step. This was the biggest gain, because the update was limited by memory bandwidth.\n- **Overlapping steps:** the next diagonal block is updated and factored first, and the next panel is solved while the rest of the update is still running. The threads wait for each other only once per step, using a busy-wait barrier.\n- **Generation and validation** are also parallelized. The generated matrix is exactly the same as before.\n\n**Two machine-level things the speed depends on.** Without them, runs were 1.5–10× slower and erratic:\n- **Thread pinning:** at startup the program pins each OpenMP thread to its own CPU, unless you set `OMP_PROC_BIND`, `OMP_PLACES` or `GOMP_CPU_AFFINITY` yourself.\n- **NUMA balancing:** the kernel's automatic NUMA balancing was moving memory pages during the timed run. The program now sets each thread's memory policy to \"local\" via a raw system call, which places memory the same way but stops that page movement. No libnuma is needed.\n\n**Behaviour you might notice**\n- **Results differ from the original in the last digit or so** (for example, the hash in `-r` output changes), because sums are added in a different order. They are identical regardless of thread count. Validation error stays small (about 1e-9 relative at n=2048).\n- **The diagonal solve multiplies by 1/diagonal instead of dividing,** a standard speed trick that can differ by at most one rounding step per operation.\n- **The \"not positive definite\" error reports the same diagonal index as the original.** I checked 33 cases with the failure placed at block boundaries. That testing caught and fixed a hang that only happened with 256 threads.\n\n**CMake:** it now requires OpenMP (`find_package(OpenMP REQUIRED)`) and links `OpenMP::OpenMP_CXX`. There are no new external dependencies and the build has no warnings.\n\nThe block sizes are tuned for this machine; other hardware may want different values."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":808,"cache_read_input_tokens":187253,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":808},"output_tokens":8,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7b9b5f59-c6f9-4eeb-b86b-39932be04df5","uuid":"4749bd41-f17c-4d98-97cf-0cdaacbec9b8","timestamp":"2026-10-04T08:03:03.338Z","request_id":"req_011Cfgr8MbvRX1R8esqWRCzZ"}
